main_text.p: Pater in Symbolo dicitur Omnipotens Creator Cœli & Terræ. Credendum itaque in Patrem Omnipotentem Creatorem omnium bonorum, Omnisapientem Gubernatorem Bonorum & Malorum, misericordem datorem Filii sui in Servatorem.Omnipoten-tem Creato-rem.
1. Deus enim in principio res omnes bonas, partim ex nihilo, partim ex materia ab ipso creata solo verbo potentiæ suæ fecit, Gen. cap.1. & 2. Psalm. 33. v.6. & 9. Hebr. 11. v. 3. 2. Pet. 3. v. 5.

2. Deus etiam res singulas à se conditas omnésque illarum actiones sapientissimè gubernat, mala etiam fieri permittit, iisq; justissimè uti novit ad electorum suorum salutem & impiorum pœnam. Exod. 21. v. 13. Devt. 9. v. 4. Poverb. 16. verf. 33. Matth. 10. verf. 29. 30. Luc. 12. v. 6. 7. &c.
3. Sic verò Deus Pater dilexit Mundum, ut unigenitum filium suum dederit (in Salvatorem) ut omnis qui credit in eum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam, Johannis 3.

page.notes: The handwritten "217" at the top right is not printed and is left out. The page number at the right of the running head is read as "9" (old form of the numeral); it is a doubtful reading. The marginal note at the top right is set in two lines with printed hyphens and is transcribed as one note at the start of the paragraph.
